findings.title: Unlimited liability carve-out for data incidents
findings.deviation: Clause 8.2 carves out all indemnification and compliance obligations in Article 8 from any liability cap, resulting in unlimited liability for privacy events and HIPAA violations.
findings.impact: AtliQ faces uncapped financial exposure for security incidents and regulatory violations.
findings.quote: The obligations of Business Associate under this Article 8 are not subject to any limitation or exclusion of liability, and shall apply notwithstanding any limitation of liability in the Master Services Agreement.
findings.counterPosition: Subject data-protection and privacy-related liabilities to a super-cap of 2x fees rather than leaving them entirely uncapped.

findings.title: Cyber insurance requirement exceeds current coverage
findings.deviation: Clause 8.3 requires AtliQ to maintain cyber liability insurance of at least $5,000,000 per claim and in the aggregate, whereas AtliQ's actual coverage limit is $1,000,000.
findings.impact: AtliQ would commit to an insurance limit it does not currently hold, leading to contract non-compliance upon signing.
findings.quote: Business Associate shall maintain, throughout the term of this BAA and for three (3) years thereafter, cyber liability and network security and privacy insurance with limits of not less than Five Million U.S. Dollars ($5,000,000) per claim and in the aggregate, covering notification costs, regulatory defense and penalties, and third-party claims arising from Privacy Events, and shall name Covered Entity as an additional insured.
findings.counterPosition: Align the required cyber insurance limit with AtliQ's current coverage of $1,000,000 per claim and in the aggregate.

findings.title: Absolute restriction on offshore access and personnel
findings.deviation: Clause 4.1 prohibits any access or processing of PHI from outside the US, and Clause 4.2 restricts subcontractors to US-based entities and personnel, preventing the use of AtliQ's offshore delivery model.
findings.impact: AtliQ is prevented from utilizing its Indian affiliate or offshore resources for any part of the services involving PHI.
findings.quote: Business Associate shall not, and shall ensure that no Subcontractor shall, access, view, create, receive, maintain, transmit, store or process PHI from or at any location outside the United States, whether directly or by remote access.
findings.counterPosition: Amend the BAA to allow remote access and processing from AtliQ's offshore location in India, subject to agreed security protocols and sub-agreements.

findings.title: One-way uncapped indemnity for privacy events
findings.deviation: Clause 8.1 establishes a unilateral indemnity requiring AtliQ to cover 'any and all losses' relating to privacy events and contract non-compliance, without fault requirements or reciprocity.
findings.impact: AtliQ must indemnify the client for all losses associated with privacy events even if the client's own negligence contributed to the event.
findings.quote: Business Associate shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Covered Entity, its Affiliates and their respective trustees, officers, employees and agents from and against any and all Losses arising out of or relating to (a) any Privacy Event involving Business Associate or any Subcontractor; (b) any breach of this BAA by Business Associate or any Subcontractor; or (c) any violation of HIPAA or Texas Privacy Law by Business Associate or any Subcontractor...
findings.counterPosition: Make the indemnity mutual where appropriate, limit AtliQ's indemnification to losses directly caused by its own default or negligence, and ensure it does not cover losses caused by the client's own negligence.

fine.note: Ownership of PHI remains with the client, which is standard and does not impact AtliQ's rights to its background IP.
No set-off provisions are included in the agreement, which matches the standard.
No delay penalties or liquidated damages are specified in this agreement.
Termination for default of the BAA is standard and does not conflict with the MSA's payment-for-work-done standard on convenience termination.
